items.heading: IICRC
items.text: Publishes the S520 standard for professional mold remediation. Confirm a company's technicians hold real, current IICRC certification before you hire them.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 2.5s6 7 6 11.5a6 6 0 0 1-12 0c0-4.5 6-11.5 6-11.5z"/></svg>
items.heading: EPA
items.text: The federal government's own guidance on identifying, cleaning up, and preventing mold growth in a home.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="12" cy="9" r="5"/><path d="M9 13.5 7.5 21 12 18.5 16.5 21 15 13.5"/></svg>
items.heading: ACAC
items.text: An independently accredited certifying body for mold inspectors and consultants — one of the few in this field whose standards are verified by an outside accreditation board, not just self-declared.

items.icon: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M12 21s-7-4.5-9.5-9A5.5 5.5 0 0 1 12 6a5.5 5.5 0 0 1 9.5 6c-2.5 4.5-9.5 9-9.5 9z"/><path d="M9 12h2v-2h2v2h2v2h-2v2h-2v-2H9z"/></svg>
items.heading: CDC
items.text: Covers the health effects of mold exposure and safe cleanup practices, separate from the remediation work itself — useful if anyone in the home has respiratory symptoms.

items.heading: BBB
items.text: Look up any mold remediation company's complaint history, customer reviews, and accreditation status — a free, independent check before you hire.
